papers.title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
papers.abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. We prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and deduce the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound.

papers.title: Graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues, one of which is zero
papers.abstract: Koolen, Hayat and Iqbal asked for the connected graphs whose distance matrix has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, the middle one being $0$. The examples they gave, namely the Johnson graphs, the Hamming graphs and the halved cubes, are distance-regular. In this note, we show that the distance spectrum of such a graph is $\{\rho,0,-c\}$ with integers $c\ge2$ and $c\mid\rho$. For $c=2$ the graphs are exactly the cocktail party graphs, and for $c=3$ they are exactly the Cartesian product $K_3\,\square\,K_3$ of two triangles, the Petersen graph and its complement. We also show that such a graph need not be transmission-regular: Seidel switching the lattice graph $K_6\,\square\,K_6$ with respect to a line and the triangular graph $T(11)$ with respect to a maximal clique of size $10$ gives graphs on $36$ and $55$ vertices with distance spectra $\{54,0^{(26)},(-6)^{(9)}\}$ and $\{81,0^{(45)},(-9)^{(9)}\}$. Among the graphs of diameter $2$ obtained by switching a strongly regular graph with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ with respect to one part of an equitable partition, these two are the only ones that have exactly three distance eigenvalues and are not transmission-regular. We also observe that the transmission-regular graphs with exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues, the smallest one being $-3$, are exactly the complements of the strongly regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ other than the cocktail party graphs.

papers.title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
papers.abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.

papers.title: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242
papers.abstract: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Mullet code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, and the determination of $\rho(1,9)$ is a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $\rho(1,9)=242$, leveraging the classification of the $349$ orbits in $\text{RM}(3,9)/\text{RM}(2,9)$ under $\text{GL}(9,2)$ [1,3]. The notebook to verify the computer search portion, Verify_RM(1,9).ipynb, contains all data and recomputes each check, and may be found in the repository this https URL.

papers.title: Combinatorial Algorithms for Partial Inverse Min-Max Spanning Tree Problem under the Weighted Sum Hamming Distance
papers.abstract: Given a connected weighted graph G=(V, E, w) and a forest F of G, the goal of partial inverse min-max spanning tree problem is to change the weight function as little as possible, so that there is a min-max spanning tree with respect to the new weight function containing F. In this paper, we study this problem under the weighted sum Hamming distance. We take the alternative set of the maximum edge weight in F with respect to the optimal weight function as a key factor, and further consider the case of this problem under the restriction of this factor. On this basis, a polynomial time algorithm with time complexity O(|V|^4) is proposed to solve this problem.
